title: Implement console musl effect bridge and reversible lifted device state for rung 3
description:
Dialect @023f5a7 §11.2: "`bennett-runtimes`' musl maps system calls onto the markers:"; row write(1,...), write(2,...), writev on fds 1/2 maps to console.write. §11.3: "In an L variant, an effect marker call becomes a call of the runtimes function `__bennett_dev_<model>_<op>` with the same operands." Console row: "`write(p, len)`: copy the first min(len, L − n) bytes to buffer[n…], n += that count; further bytes are discarded with the oracle's other writes". R uses ISA effect/tape (§11.1/11.2), not L's truncated buffer or CC host writes.

Exact publication audit:
/usr/lib/llvm-18/bin/llvm-nm --defined-only /home/tobias/Projects/bennett-workspace/bennett-conformance/.tmp/rung3-bennett-runtimes-6808622d560b2e301c635c205eecde3d932b6df5/dist/llvm18/bennett-runtimes.bc
(and LLVM 23 counterpart). Exports lack __bennett_dev_console_write and printf/puts/write/exit; device-models and libc-shims contain README skeletons only. Gate reports runtime libc/console publication missing.

Fixed means: provide the console marker bridge and ordinary bitcode __bennett_dev_console_write/state with §11.3 binding rules, no-binding fault and reversal; retain R effect tape semantics and reset through actual executors. Add console/native-comparison support without defining production marker symbols or using host libc. A publication audit alone does not establish the hello-world route. Estimated size medium (480 minutes).

Evidence: /home/tobias/Projects/bennett-workspace/bennett-conformance/.tmp/rung-3/20261101T125019.671846Z (report.json, exact argv and per-command stdout/stderr). North Star §8 rung 3 remains full ordinary musl printf hello-world, R console, reset and deterministic saved-tape replay; no freestanding replacement, host-libc comparison or fake marker definition is acceptable. These are prerequisites, not downstream corpus verdicts.
close_reason: scripts/gate PASS for both major publications: actual musl syscall -> undefined console marker route; ordinary lifted bound state; oracle truncation/action preflight faults; published-model store-history reversal and deterministic native-model tape replay/tamper checks. R keeps ISA tape, no production marker body. End-to-end executor reset/replay remains rung-3 conformance, not established by native tests. State/tier/exit responsibilities documented.

title: Publish Bennett musl sysroots and hello-world libc/native-comparison closure for LLVM 18/23
description:
Dialect 0.2.10 @023f5a7 §1.5: "with `rmode=` against the `bennett-runtimes` musl sysroot, for which the checker's seeds stand in". §19.1: "The driver links all bitcode inputs (§19.8), links `bennett-runtimes` and `bennett-arith` bitcode of the link's major M, runs the post-link pipeline (`lto<O3>` by default, or any envelope pipeline of §21.1 the user selects), then runs the plugin on the whole program (NS §3.3)." §17.7 requires materialised code "linked with `bennett-runtimes` and `bennett-arith` (never host libc or libm)".

Observed exact command:
/usr/lib/llvm-18/bin/clang --target=x86_64-unknown-linux-musl --sysroot=/home/tobias/Projects/bennett-workspace/bennett-runtimes/dist/llvm18/musl-sysroot -nostdinc -isystem /home/tobias/Projects/bennett-workspace/bennett-runtimes/dist/llvm18/musl-sysroot/include -O2 -flto -emit-llvm -c /home/tobias/Projects/bennett-workspace/bennett-conformance/ladder/rung-3/fixtures/hello.c -o /home/tobias/Projects/bennett-workspace/bennett-conformance/.tmp/rung-3/20261101T125019.671846Z/18/input.bc
(and the recorded LLVM 23 counterpart). Both fail: fatal error: 'stdio.h' file not found. The default dist/llvm<M>/musl-sysroot path is consumer glue, not a spec-mandated layout; --sysroot18/23 can override it. Published dist bitcode only has malloc/calloc/free/memset/memmove closure, no stdio.

Fixed means: publish a real musl sysroot (headers, LLVM-major bitcode and startup/comparison support), implement the ordinary printf/write/stdio flush/exit closure and optimizer-created puts without delegating to host libc. Compile the exact hello.c, link runtime+arith before lto<O3>/plugin, and supply an auditable §17.7 native link. Scope is the first rung-3 slice of brt-q1k/brt-zct, not a freestanding seed. Estimated size large (1440 minutes).

Evidence: /home/tobias/Projects/bennett-workspace/bennett-conformance/.tmp/rung-3/20261101T125019.671846Z (report.json, exact argv and per-command stdout/stderr). North Star §8 rung 3 remains full ordinary musl printf hello-world, R console, reset and deterministic saved-tape replay; no freestanding replacement, host-libc comparison or fake marker definition is acceptable. These are prerequisites, not downstream corpus verdicts.
close_reason: Pinned musl 1.2.5 combined LLVM 18/23 publication, headers, static comparison startup/syscall transport and published allocator integration. scripts/gate PASS: byte-reproduced sysroots/bitcode; ordinary hello and formatted printf/atexit/flush static native links have no unresolved or dynamic imports. Device syscall bridge follows in brt-cgb; full DR families remain brt-zct/q1k.

title: Rung 2: publish LLVM18/23 allocator and libc bitcode closure for the C hashtable
description:
Rung 2 input: the complete hashtable.c / main_golden.c corpus copied to bennett-conformance/ladder/rung-2/fixtures (original SHA-256 8cbd5a3698aea0da1f7187b97be34a0ed33743394f045c49c943323f94abd4b9). It calls malloc/free; clang -O2 and lto<O3> also form calloc and llvm.memset. Before the production plugin, the driver must link runtimes bitcode for the LLVM major. This repo currently has only src/allocator/bump.c defining bennett_alloc/bennett_free; no .bc files, no malloc/free/calloc shim or LLVM18/23 distribution/build entry point. The gate's concrete failure is `missing runtimes bitcode for LLVM <18|23>: <repo>/dist/llvm<18|23>/bennett-runtimes.bc (dialect §19.1)`.

Determining accepted dialect 0.2.10 @023f5a7 §19.1 sentence: "The driver links all bitcode inputs (§19.8), links bennett-runtimes and bennett-arith bitcode of the link's major M, runs the post-link pipeline (lto<O3> by default, or any envelope pipeline of §21.1 the user selects), then runs the plugin on the whole program (NS §3.3)." Formatting omitted only. §4.5 item 2 resolves a runtime shim as a definition in these bitcode libraries, an ordinary device function. §17.1: "shadow-stack frames and heap allocations are zero-filled in both builds; globals hold their initialisers." §17.7 requires the materialised native comparison binary linked with bennett-runtimes/bennett-arith, never host libc/libm.

Fixed means: publish reproducible, major-matched runtimes bitcode with the allocator/libc closure needed by the exact corpus (including optimizer-produced calloc), reaching the specified primitives with deterministic zero-fill, bounds, null/free and allocation-history semantics, plus the corresponding native comparison support. Make the gate's explicit runtime-link stage pass on LLVM18 and23 and rerun without replacing heap operations by a checksum summary or silently using host libc. Filename is gate-configurable; dist/llvmM/bennett-runtimes.bc is a consumer default, not a spec-mandated name. Keep implementation in this owning repo; rung2 only links/consumes the published artifact. Estimated size medium for this allocator-only slice; broader runtime remains separate.

A prior corpus-only plugin probe also timed out in the reference-analysis path (plugin bp-au6), but that incomplete link is NOT full §19.1 pipeline evidence. It must be rerun against the runtime-linked module after this prerequisite. The gate now distinguishes required pipeline stages from explicitly named corpus-only diagnostic probes. No runtime source implementation is authorized in the rung2 implementation slice.
notes:
Implementation milestones: 469246e publishes malloc/calloc/free, native memset and N26 helpers for LLVM18/23; 57108a2 adds reproducibility/export/link/LTO/native-golden gate and pushed-commit hook. Red: absent publication/backend; then native closure audit caught a host memset leak after --only-needed discarded the ABI definition. Green: retain complete runtime at native codegen; no allocator/memory dynamic imports, ten golden cases on both majors, exact saved/fresh postlink closure, seven trap scenarios each. Clean detached-checkout pre-push gate also passes byte-identically. Alignment contract question filed/committed in dialect b-dialect-spec-jjr (fc050a6); future runtime/libc tracked brt-zct/brt-q1k. Consumer gate started once against plugin c4ffcd3be30bf7ef9a354a4771aeaa237cd636ed; final table pending.
Final consumer run 20261031T223029.611386Z exited 1: runtime bitcode link and post-link LTO PASS on LLVM18 and LLVM23. Actual consumer postlink non-intrinsic declarations are only __bennett_qalloc/qfree and __bennett_nz_alloc/free/fault. Both production passes exit124 after300 seconds, bp-au6; every launch/admission/forward/reverse stage BLOCKED downstream. Evidence ../bennett-conformance/.tmp/rung-2/20261031T223029.611386Z/{table.md,report.json}. Local gate and clean-checkout pre-push gate at88058b0 PASS, including byte-identical publication, actual arith links, all ten native cases per major, no host allocation/memory shims. Native comparison support tested; full driver-materialised comparison/execution remains consumer scope.
close_reason: Published reproducible LLVM18/23 allocator/libc closure; local/clean-checkout gates pass; consumer runtime-link and LTO PASS on both majors. Downstream production timeouts remain bp-au6.

title: Make LLVM 23 local-symbol GUIDs independent of checkout path
description: Detached pre-push on 095aa2c failed byte comparison only for LLVM 23. Comparing disassembly shows !guid metadata of internal musl globals/functions hashes absolute input translation-unit names before source_filename is normalised. Same-root scripts/gate did not expose it. Compile source inputs relative to an explicit build cwd, and add relocated-source byte comparisons to scripts/gate; keep meaningful GUIDs rather than stripping metadata.
notes: After stable-GUID relocation PASS, detached pre-push exposed a test-only dependency-root bug: test_musl.py hardcoded ROOT.parent/bennett-arith instead of respecting BENNETT_ARITH_ROOT already exported by pre-push. Fixed to match native-link and existing publication tests; rerun required.
close_reason: Relocated-source bytes and full scripts/gate PASS; detached test dependency root also corrected to respect BENNETT_ARITH_ROOT. Both failures and fixes recorded in HANDOFF.

title: Driver consumer: publish freestanding comparison startup/libc/primitive and sanitizer closure
description: Driver M1 cyg.3 implements §17.7/§19.5 strict native links: materialised device.bc plus major-matched bennett-runtimes.bc/bennett-arith.bc, -nostdlib -nostdinc -static -no-pie. Current exports (rung-2-allocation-v1) lack _start, printf/musl closure and native primitive definitions in publication; native heap.c exists comparison-only but hardcodes heap base 0x10000000 and capacities, not the device resolved layout. Link refuses instead of host libc/libm fallback. Need published native startup and primitive closure with configurable matching device layout/capacities, full musl printf, and a usable freestanding ASan/UBSan closure or specified instrumentation adapter (normal sanitizer default linking imports host libc/libm and cannot be used). Corpus remains unmodified hashtable.c/main_golden.c and rung-3 hello.c; no marker replacement or private libc substitute. Both majors tested with loud strict link failures; driver emits argv and error logs.

title: Extend libc allocation/string/memory coverage beyond the measured hashtable closure
description: Dialect 0.2.10 @023f5a7 §4.5 item 2 promises libc/musl runtime shims; §5.1 allocation reference list includes realloc, aligned_alloc, posix_memalign, memalign, strdup, strndup, C++ new, Rust and Julia allocators. brt-3sa measured both saved postlink.ll modules: only malloc/free/calloc plus llvm.memset, not realloc/memcpy/memmove/strlen libc calls. Published N26 helpers cover memmove/memset and native memset. Implement the remaining actual libc entry points and wider musl slice, with overflow/zero-fill/liveness semantics and independent tests, after resolving alignment question b-dialect-spec-jjr. No host libc delegation; capability is deferred, not rejected.

title: Complete runtime DR surface beyond the rung-2 allocation slice
description: Accepted dialect 0.2.10 @023f5a7 §1.2: "define every entry point that §11, §13, §14, §17 and §20 name ... with the semantics stated there, as ordinary bitcode compiled by the same pipeline; suites DR and DF". This publication stages only the rung-2 allocation/libc closure and N26 memory helpers; full runtime conformance remains required, never narrowed. Implement §11 coherent console/clock/entropy/block state and models, musl syscall/VFS shims; §12.8 integer helper families; §13.5 __bennett_rt_fenv and fenv functions (arith owns softfloat); §14 trampoline/EH/SJLJ/fiber/blockaddress machinery; §17.3 shadow stack logical lifetimes/checks plus entry replay; §20 RAM/CSR/MMIO/poll/Sv39/platform context machinery. Each needs independent contract vectors and same-major native materialised comparison tests. Do not substitute trap stubs for promised capabilities.
notes: Rung-3 console/musl slice completed in brt-1ft/brt-cgb. Remaining VFS/device/thread/runtime families retain this epic scope. Driver must materialise N28–N30 returning exit/EH helper and declare bounded action undo history; native-model tests do not establish executor whole-program conformance. Dialect integration reading b-dialect-spec-lbq.
